answer: In an agent economy selling gale forecasts, opal appraisals, and umber pigments, each agent must lock collateral for 30 days to vote on marketplace rules, with voting power proportional to its deposit. Creating a thousand identities gives an attacker no more influence than putting the same funds in one account. To gain a majority, the attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined, sacrificing liquidity and other uses of that money.
